name: Mathematics
tagline: From counting pebbles to the edge of the unknown.

nodes.title: Counting
nodes.goal: Count objects to 10 and back.
nodes.kid_text: Counting means giving each thing its very own number word. Touch the first teddy and say "one," the next and say "two," all the way up to ten. When you want to go back down, count like a rocket: ten, nine, eight, blast off! Every thing gets exactly one number, and you never skip.

lesson_media.alt: Ten blue-grey pebbles arranged in two rows of five.
lesson_media.caption: Touch each pebble once as you count. The last number word tells how many are in the whole set.

lesson_media.title: Count each pebble once
lesson_media.instructions: Touch every pebble once. Then mix the same pebbles and notice what changes — and what does not.

quiz.prompt: How many? 🍎🍎🍎
quiz.say: How many apples do you see? Is it 2, 3, or 4?
quiz.explain: Yes! One, two, three apples, one number for each apple.

quiz.prompt: Count the stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
quiz.say: Let's count the stars together. Are there 4, 5, or 6?
quiz.explain: There are five stars, and we never skip one.

quiz.prompt: 10, 9, 8, then what? 🚀
quiz.say: We are counting down like a rocket. Ten, nine, eight, and then what comes next? 7, 5, or 11?
quiz.explain: After eight comes seven, and soon we blast off!

quiz.prompt: How many fish? 🐟🐟🐟🐟
quiz.say: How many fish do you see? Is it 3, 4, or 5?
quiz.explain: Touch each fish and count: one, two, three, four!

quiz.prompt: Count the balloons 🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈
quiz.say: Let's count these balloons together. Is it 8, 6, or 7?
quiz.explain: There are seven balloons, one number word for each one.

quiz.prompt: 5, 4, 3, then what? 🚀
quiz.say: We are counting down: five, four, three, and then what comes next? 2, 1, or 6?
quiz.explain: Counting back, two comes right after three.

quiz.prompt: Which shows 2 cats?
quiz.say: Which picture shows exactly two cats? Three cats, two cats, or one cat?
quiz.explain: Two cats means you count one, two, and then stop.

nodes.title: Shapes All Around
nodes.goal: Name circles, triangles, squares and count their sides.
nodes.kid_text: Shapes are hiding everywhere you look! A circle is perfectly round like a pizza, with no corners at all. A triangle has 3 straight sides and 3 pointy corners, like a slice of that pizza. A square has 4 sides that are all the same length, like a window. Trace each edge with your finger to count the sides.

lesson_media.alt: A round plate, a triangular sail, and a square wooden window stand side by side.
lesson_media.caption: A shape keeps its outline wherever you find it: round plate, triangular sail, square window.

lesson_media.title: Turn the shape wheel
lesson_media.instructions: Choose a shape, then show its corners. Count where two straight sides meet.

quiz.prompt: Which one is round? 🔴 🔺 🟦
quiz.say: Which shape is perfectly round with no corners, like a pizza? The circle, the triangle, or the square?
quiz.explain: The circle is round all the way around, with no corners at all.

quiz.prompt: How many sides? 🔺
quiz.say: Trace the triangle with your finger. How many straight sides does it have? 3, 4, or 5?
quiz.explain: A triangle has three straight sides and three pointy corners.

quiz.prompt: Which has 4 same sides? 🟦 🔵 🔺
quiz.say: Which shape has four sides that are all the same length, like a window? The square, the circle, or the triangle?
quiz.explain: The square has four sides, and every side is the same.

quiz.prompt: How many sides? 🟦
quiz.say: How many sides does this square have? 3, 4, or 6?
quiz.explain: A square has four sides, all the same length.

quiz.prompt: How many corners? 🔺
quiz.say: How many pointy corners does this triangle have? 3, 4, or 0?
quiz.explain: A triangle has three pointy corners, one for each side to meet.

quiz.prompt: Which shape has no corners?
quiz.say: Which one of these has no corners at all? The square, the triangle, or the circle?
quiz.explain: A circle is smooth and round, so it has no corners.

quiz.prompt: Which one is a triangle?
quiz.say: Which one of these is a triangle? The purple square, the white circle, or the red pointy one?
quiz.explain: The pointy one with three sides is the triangle.

nodes.title: Bigger and Smaller
nodes.goal: Compare numbers and sizes.
nodes.kid_text: You can tell which pile has more by matching the objects one to one. Put the blocks in two equally spaced rows, with each block directly across from one in the other row. If one row has blocks left unmatched, that set has more. Size is a different comparison: one elephant is bigger than one mouse, even though both sets contain one animal.

quiz.prompt: Which is bigger? 🐘 🐭
quiz.say: Which one is bigger, the elephant or the mouse?
quiz.explain: The elephant is much bigger than the tiny mouse.

quiz.prompt: More cookies? 🍪🍪 or 🍪🍪🍪🍪
quiz.say: One plate has two cookies and one plate has four cookies. Which plate has more?
quiz.explain: Four is more than two, so that plate has more cookies.

quiz.prompt: Which number is smaller?
quiz.say: Which number is smaller: 2, 8, or 5?
quiz.explain: Two is smaller, because we say it first when we count.

quiz.prompt: Which is smaller? 🐜 🐕
quiz.say: Which one is smaller, the tiny ant or the big dog?
quiz.explain: An ant is much smaller than a dog.

quiz.prompt: Fewer ducks? 🦆🦆🦆 or 🦆
quiz.say: Which side has fewer ducks? Three ducks, or just one duck?
quiz.explain: One duck is fewer than three ducks.

quiz.prompt: Which number is bigger?
quiz.say: Which number is bigger: 4, 9, or 7?
quiz.explain: Nine is bigger because it comes later when you count.

quiz.prompt: Which is heavier? 🐘 🪶
quiz.say: Which is heavier, the elephant or the little feather?
quiz.explain: An elephant is very heavy, and a feather is very light.

lesson_media.alt: Five counters are paired with five of seven counters, leaving two unmatched in the larger set.
lesson_media.caption: Pairing one object from each set proves that seven is two more than five. Size and spacing do not change how many objects a set contains.

nodes.title: Patterns
nodes.goal: See what comes next in a repeating or growing pattern.
nodes.kid_text: Some patterns repeat in the same order, like red, blue, red, blue. Find the repeating unit and you can predict what comes next: after red, blue, red comes blue. Other patterns grow, like 1, 2, 3, adding one more each step. You can say a pattern, point to it, or build it with objects to test its rule.

quiz.say: Red, blue, red, blue, red. What comes next: blue, red, or yellow?
quiz.explain: Red then blue keeps repeating, so blue comes next.

quiz.say: Cat, cat, dog. Cat, cat, dog. Cat, cat. What comes next: the dog, the cat, or the mouse?
quiz.explain: Two cats then a dog is the beat, so a dog comes next.

quiz.say: One, two, three, four. This pattern grows by one each time. What comes next? 5, 1, or 7?
quiz.explain: Each step adds one more, so five comes next.

quiz.say: Green, yellow, green, yellow, green, yellow. What comes next: green, yellow, or blue?
quiz.explain: The pattern goes back to green each time after yellow.

quiz.answer: stomp
quiz.say: Clap, stomp, clap, stomp, clap. What comes next: a stomp, a clap, or a jump?
quiz.explain: After every clap comes a stomp, so it is stomp.

quiz.say: Apple, apple, banana, apple, apple, banana, apple. What comes next: an apple, a banana, or some grapes?
quiz.explain: Two apples always come before the banana, so another apple is next.

quiz.say: Two, four, six, eight. What comes next? 9, 10, or 12?
quiz.explain: This pattern grows by two each time, so ten comes next.

lesson_media.alt: An alternating circle-square unit repeats three times above groups of one, two, three, and four leaves.
lesson_media.caption: Some patterns repeat a smallest unit; others grow by a stated rule. A sequence is predictable only after its rule is identified.

nodes.title: Numbers to Twenty
nodes.goal: Read and order numbers up to 20.
nodes.kid_text: After ten comes a whole new team of numbers, all the way to twenty! Say them in order: eleven, twelve, thirteen, and each one is just one bigger than the last. If you line up cards from 1 to 20, the small numbers sit on the left and the big ones on the right. The farther right you go, the more it counts.

quiz.prompt: What comes after 12?
quiz.say: When we count, what number comes right after twelve? 13, 11, or 20?
quiz.explain: Twelve, then thirteen, just one bigger.

quiz.prompt: Missing number: 11, 12, ?, 14
quiz.say: Eleven, twelve, hmm, fourteen. Which number is missing? 13, 15, or 10?
quiz.explain: Thirteen sits right between twelve and fourteen.

quiz.prompt: Which number is bigger?
quiz.say: Which number is bigger: 17, 9, or 13?
quiz.explain: Seventeen is bigger, because it comes later when we count.

quiz.prompt: What comes before 15?
quiz.say: Which number comes right before fifteen? 16, 14, or 13?
quiz.explain: Fourteen is one less than fifteen, so it comes first.

quiz.prompt: Missing number: 17, 18, ?, 20
quiz.say: Seventeen, eighteen, hmm, twenty. Which number is missing? 19, 21, or 16?
quiz.explain: Nineteen fits right between eighteen and twenty.

quiz.prompt: Which number is smaller?
quiz.say: Which number is smaller: 20, 11, or 15?
quiz.explain: Eleven is smaller because it comes first when you count.

quiz.prompt: Which one says sixteen?
quiz.say: Which one of these is the number sixteen? 6, 60, or 16?
quiz.explain: Sixteen is written with a one and a six, like this: sixteen.

lesson_media.alt: A full ten-frame and six counters in a second frame represent the number sixteen.
lesson_media.caption: Sixteen is one group of ten and six more. Its numeral comes after 15 and before 17.

nodes.title: Addition
nodes.goal: Add numbers up to 100 quickly and surely.
nodes.kid_text: Adding means putting groups together to find how many you have in all. If you have 5 stickers and a friend gives you 3 more, count on: six, seven, eight, so you have 8! You can add in any order, so 3 + 5 also makes 8. A tens trick helps: 8 + 5 is the same as 10 + 3, which is 13.

lesson_media.alt: A ten-frame holds eight blue pebbles and two of five green counters; three green counters remain below.
lesson_media.caption: Use 2 from the 5 to complete ten; 3 remain, so 8 + 5 = 13.

lesson_media.title: Make a friendly ten
lesson_media.instructions: Move counters from one addend to fill the ten-frame. Swap the addends and notice that the total stays the same.

quiz.say: Five plus three. Is it 7, 8, or 9?
quiz.explain: Count on from five: six, seven, eight!

quiz.say: Eight plus five. Is it 12, 13, or 14?
quiz.explain: Eight and two make ten, and three more makes thirteen.

quiz.say: Twenty plus thirty. Is it 40, 50, or 60?
quiz.explain: Two tens and three tens make five tens, which is fifty.

quiz.say: What is six plus four? 9, 10, or 11?
quiz.explain: Six and four make a friendly ten.

quiz.say: What is seven plus seven? 14, 12, or 15?
quiz.explain: Double seven is fourteen.

quiz.say: What is twenty-five plus ten? 30, 45, or 35?
quiz.explain: Twenty-five is two tens and five ones. One more ten makes three tens and five ones: thirty-five.

quiz.say: Three plus six is nine. So what is six plus three? 9, 6, or 8?
quiz.explain: Swapping the two numbers round never changes the answer, so 6 + 3 is 9 as well.

nodes.title: Subtraction
nodes.goal: Take away and find the difference.
nodes.kid_text: Subtraction is taking some away and counting what is left. If you have 9 grapes and eat 4, then 5 grapes are still waiting. It also answers "how many more?": if you have 9 and a friend has 4, you have 5 more. Subtraction undoes adding, so because 4 + 5 = 9, we know 9 - 4 = 5.

quiz.say: Nine take away four. Is it 4, 5, or 6?
quiz.explain: You had nine grapes, ate four, and five are still waiting.

quiz.prompt: 7 sweets, eat 2. Left? 🍬
quiz.say: You have seven sweets and you eat two of them. How many are left? 4, 5, or 6?
quiz.explain: Seven take away two leaves five sweets.

quiz.prompt: You have 10, friend has 6. How many more?
quiz.say: You have ten stickers and your friend has six. How many more do you have? 3, 4, or 5?
quiz.explain: Ten take away six is four, so you have four more.

quiz.say: What is eight take away three? 4, 5, or 6?
quiz.explain: Start at eight and count back three: seven, six, five.

quiz.prompt: 6 birds 🐦, 2 fly away. Left?
quiz.say: There were six birds and two flew away. How many are left? 4, 3, or 8?
quiz.explain: Six take away two leaves four birds sitting there.

quiz.say: What is twelve take away five? 6, 8, or 7?
quiz.explain: Twelve minus five leaves seven.

quiz.say: Six plus three is nine. So what is nine take away three? 3, 6, or 9?
quiz.explain: Taking away undoes adding, so you land back on six.

lesson_media.alt: Nine counters with four crossed out leave five; paired rows of nine and four also differ by five.
lesson_media.caption: The equation 9 − 4 = 5 can describe what remains or the difference between two quantities. Addition checks the result because 4 + 5 = 9.

nodes.title: Place Value
nodes.goal: Know what each digit in a big number means.
nodes.kid_text: In a big number, where a digit sits tells you how much it is worth. In 47, the 4 means 4 tens, which is forty, and the 7 means 7 ones. So 47 is really 40 and 7 packed together. The digit itself does not grow: moving it one place left makes its place value ten times as large.

quiz.prompt: In 47, what is the 4 worth?
quiz.say: In the number forty-seven, what is the four worth? 4, 40, or 400?
quiz.explain: The four sits in the tens spot, so it means four tens, which is forty.

quiz.prompt: How many tens in 60?
quiz.say: How many tens are hiding inside sixty? 6, 16, or 60?
quiz.explain: Six tens stack up to make sixty.

quiz.prompt: 40 and 7 together make?
quiz.say: Forty and seven packed together. Is it 47, 74, or 11?
quiz.explain: Forty and seven make forty-seven.

quiz.prompt: In 58, what is the 8 worth?
quiz.say: In the number fifty-eight, how much is the eight worth? 8, 80, or 58?
quiz.explain: The 8 is in the ones place, so it is worth just 8. The 5 is the one worth 50.

quiz.prompt: How many tens in 30?
quiz.say: How many tens are inside thirty? 30, 3, or 13?
quiz.explain: Thirty is three tens stacked together.

quiz.prompt: Which number has 9 tens?
quiz.say: Which number has nine tens in it? 9, 19, or 90?
quiz.explain: Ninety is nine tens, so the nine sits in the tens spot.

quiz.prompt: 20 and 6 together make?
quiz.say: What do twenty and six make when you put them together? 62, 206, or 26?
quiz.explain: Two tens and six ones make twenty-six.

lesson_media.alt: Four ten-rods sit in the tens column and seven unit squares sit in the ones column to make 47.
lesson_media.caption: In 47, position gives the 4 a value of forty and the 7 a value of seven. One ten can be exchanged for ten ones without changing the total.

nodes.title: Multiplication
nodes.goal: Master the times tables to 12 × 12.
nodes.kid_text: Multiplying is a fast way to add the same number again and again. 4 x 3 means 4 groups of 3, so instead of 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 you just know it is 12. Picture 4 rows of 3 cookies on a tray and count them all: 12. Learn your times tables up to 12 x 12 and these answers pop out in a snap.

quiz.prompt: 4 rows of 3 🍪. How many?
quiz.say: There are four rows of cookies with three cookies in each row. How many cookies in all? 7, 9, or 12?
quiz.explain: Four groups of three make twelve cookies.

quiz.say: Two times five. Is it 7, 10, or 12?
quiz.explain: Two groups of five make ten.

quiz.say: Six times six. Is it 12, 30, or 36?
quiz.explain: Six rows of six make thirty-six.

quiz.say: What is three times three? 6, 9, or 12?
quiz.explain: Three groups of three make nine.

quiz.prompt: 5 groups of 2 🍬. How many?
quiz.say: There are five groups with two sweets in each. How many sweets in all? 10, 7, or 12?
quiz.explain: Two, four, six, eight, ten — five groups of two make ten.

quiz.say: What is twelve times twelve? 124, 144, or 122?
quiz.explain: Twelve twelves make one hundred forty-four, the last one in your tables.

quiz.say: What is seven times two? 14, 16, or 9?
quiz.explain: Two sevens are fourteen, just like seven plus seven.

lesson_media.alt: Four rows of three counters form an array of twelve; turning the array gives three rows of four.
lesson_media.caption: Four groups of three total twelve. Rotating the array shows that 4 × 3 and 3 × 4 have the same product.

nodes.title: Division
nodes.goal: Share into equal groups; divide with times-table facts.
nodes.kid_text: Dividing means sharing a bunch into equal groups so everyone gets the same amount. If you have 12 candies and 3 friends, deal them out one at a time until each friend has 4. Division is the opposite of multiplying: because 3 x 4 = 12, we know 12 / 3 = 4. Your times tables help you share fast!

quiz.prompt: 12 candies, 3 friends. Each gets?
quiz.say: Twelve candies shared fairly with three friends. How many does each friend get? 3, 4, or 6?
quiz.explain: Deal them out one at a time and each friend gets four.

quiz.say: Ten shared into two equal groups. Is it 4, 5, or 8?
quiz.explain: Ten splits into two equal groups of five.

quiz.say: Three times four is twelve. So twelve divided by four is what? 2, 3, or 4?
quiz.explain: Dividing undoes multiplying, so the answer is three.

quiz.say: What is eight shared into two equal groups? 3, 4, or 6?
quiz.explain: Eight splits fairly into two groups of four.

quiz.prompt: 6 apples 🍎, 2 baskets. Each gets?
quiz.say: Six apples go into two baskets, the same in each. How many in one basket? 3, 2, or 4?
quiz.explain: Deal them out one by one and each basket ends with three.

quiz.say: What is twenty shared into five equal groups? 5, 15, or 4?
quiz.explain: Five fours make twenty, so each group gets four.

quiz.say: Five times three is fifteen. So what is fifteen shared into five groups? 5, 3, or 10?
quiz.explain: Dividing undoes multiplying, so the answer is three.

lesson_media.alt: Twelve counters are shared equally among three bowls, leaving four counters in each bowl.
lesson_media.caption: Sharing 12 among 3 equal groups gives 4 in each group. Making groups of 3 from the same 12 instead produces 4 groups.

nodes.title: Measuring Things
nodes.goal: Measure length, mass and liquid capacity with units.
nodes.kid_text: Measuring tells you how long, how much mass, or how much liquid there is, using agreed units. Align one end of an object with the ruler's zero mark and read the mark at the other end. A scale can measure mass in grams, and a marked jug can measure liquid in millilitres. Real pencils and apples vary, so measure the object you actually have and keep using the same unit.

quiz.prompt: How long is a pencil? Use what?
quiz.say: What do you use to find out how long a pencil is? A ruler, a cup, or a scale?
quiz.explain: A ruler measures how long something is.

quiz.prompt: How heavy is an apple? Use what? 🍎
quiz.say: What do you use to find out how heavy an apple is? A scale, a ruler, or a clock?
quiz.explain: A scale tells us how heavy something is.

quiz.prompt: Start measuring at which number? 📏
quiz.say: When you lay the ruler down, which number do you start at? 0, 1, or 10?
quiz.explain: Align one end with zero and read the mark at the other end. If an object starts at a different mark, subtract the starting reading from the ending reading.

quiz.prompt: Measure the juice in a jug. Use what?
quiz.say: To find out how much juice there is, what do you use? A ruler, a clock, or a measuring cup?
quiz.explain: A measuring cup tells you how much liquid you have.

quiz.prompt: Best unit for a pencil?
quiz.answer: cm
quiz.say: What unit do we use for how long a pencil is? Is it cm, grams, or minutes?
quiz.explain: Centimetres measure length, and grams measure mass.

quiz.prompt: Milk is measured in?
quiz.answer: litres
quiz.say: Milk is measured in what? Metres, litres, or grams?
quiz.explain: Litres tell us how much liquid fits in the bottle.

quiz.prompt: Which is heavier? 🚗 🍎
quiz.say: Which weighs more, the car or the apple?
quiz.explain: A car weighs far more than one little apple.

lesson_media.alt: A pencil is aligned with a ruler, an apple rests on a scale, and water reaches a marked level in a measuring jug.
lesson_media.caption: Length, mass, and liquid volume require different instruments and units. A measurement is a number together with its unit.

nodes.title: Time and Calendars
nodes.goal: Read clocks and calendars.
nodes.kid_text: A clock has two hands that tell the time of day. The short hand points to the hour and the long hand points to the minutes as it sweeps all the way around in one hour. A calendar shows days and months: 7 days make a week, and 12 months make a year. When the short hand is on 3 and the long hand points straight up at 12, it is 3 o'clock!

quiz.prompt: Short hand on 3, long hand up. Time? ⏰
quiz.answer: 3 o'clock
quiz.say: The short hand points to the three and the long hand points straight up at the twelve. Is it 3 o'clock, 12 o'clock, or 6 o'clock?
quiz.explain: The short hand tells the hour, so it is three o'clock.

quiz.prompt: How many days in a week? 📅
quiz.say: How many days make one whole week? 5, 7, or 12?
quiz.explain: Seven days make one week, all the way round.

quiz.prompt: How many months in a year? 📅
quiz.say: How many months are in one whole year? 7, 10, or 12?
quiz.explain: Twelve months make a whole year.

quiz.prompt: Short hand on 6, long hand up. Time? ⏰
quiz.answer: 6 o'clock
quiz.say: The short hand points at six and the long hand points straight up. Is it 6 o'clock, 12 o'clock, or 9 o'clock?
quiz.explain: The short hand names the hour, so it is six o'clock.

quiz.prompt: Which hand shows the hour? 🕐
quiz.answer: short
quiz.say: On a clock, which hand tells you the hour? The long hand or the short hand?
quiz.explain: The short hand points at the hour, and the long one counts minutes.

quiz.prompt: How many hours in one day? ☀️🌙
quiz.say: How many hours are there in one whole day and night? 12, 24, or 7?
quiz.explain: A day and night together make twenty-four hours.

quiz.prompt: Which month comes after June? 📅
quiz.answer: July
quiz.say: Which month comes right after June? July, May, or April?
quiz.explain: July follows June on the calendar.

lesson_media.alt: A clock shows three o'clock with its short hour hand at 3 and long minute hand at 12, beside a calendar changing from June to July.
lesson_media.caption: At exactly 3:00, the minute hand points to 12 and the hour hand points to 3. As minutes pass, both hands move; this calendar uses the common Gregorian month sequence.

nodes.title: Halves and Quarters
nodes.goal: Split wholes into equal parts and name them.
nodes.kid_text: A fraction is what you get when you split a whole into equal parts. Cut a pizza into 2 equal pieces and each one is a half; cut it into 4 equal pieces and each is a quarter. The parts must be the same size to be fair. Two halves make a whole, and four quarters make a whole too!

quiz.prompt: Pizza cut in 2 equal parts. Each is? 🍕
quiz.answer: half
quiz.say: A pizza is cut into two equal pieces. Is each piece a half, a quarter, or a whole?
quiz.explain: Two equal pieces means each one is a half.

quiz.prompt: How many quarters make a whole?
quiz.say: How many quarters do you need to make one whole? 2, 3, or 4?
quiz.explain: Four quarters fit together to make a whole.

quiz.prompt: Fair pieces must be the same size?
quiz.answer: yes
quiz.say: For everyone to get a fair share, must all the pieces be the same size? Yes or no?
quiz.explain: Yes, fair parts are always the same size.

quiz.prompt: Cake cut in 4 equal parts. Each is? 🍰
quiz.answer: quarter
quiz.say: A cake is cut into four equal pieces. What is each piece called? A half, a quarter, or a whole?
quiz.explain: Four equal pieces means each one is a quarter.

quiz.prompt: How many halves make a whole?
quiz.say: How many halves do you need to make one whole? 2, 4, or 3?
quiz.explain: Two equal halves fit together to make one whole.

quiz.prompt: Cut a pizza in 2, or in 4. Bigger piece? 🍕
quiz.answer: half
quiz.say: One pizza is cut into two pieces and another into four. Which piece is bigger, a half or a quarter?
quiz.explain: A half is bigger because the whole is split into fewer pieces.

quiz.prompt: 2 quarters make how much? 🍕
quiz.answer: half
quiz.say: If you put two quarters together, how much do you have? A half, a whole, or a quarter?
quiz.explain: Two quarters join up to make one half.

lesson_media.alt: Two identical rectangles are divided into two equal parts and four equal parts, showing halves and quarters of the same-sized whole.
lesson_media.caption: Fraction names require equal parts of the same whole. Two halves or four quarters make one whole, and two quarters cover the same amount as one half.

nodes.title: Fractions
nodes.goal: Add, subtract, compare, multiply and simplify fractions.

lesson_media.alt: Three equal-length fraction bars show one of two, two of four and four of eight equal parts shaded, each covering exactly half of its bar.
lesson_media.caption: One half, two quarters and four eighths are equivalent fractions: the partitions change, but the shaded amount stays the same.

lesson_media.title: Build equivalent fractions
lesson_media.instructions: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the same factor. Watch the partitions change while the fraction's value stays the same.

quiz.prompt: Compute 2/3 + 1/4.
quiz.explain: Use a common denominator of 12: 2/3 = 8/12 and 1/4 = 3/12, so the sum is 11/12.

quiz.prompt: Sam says 3/8 must be bigger than 2/5, because 8 is bigger than 5. Which reply is correct?
quiz.answer: Sam is wrong: 3/8 = 15/40 and 2/5 = 16/40
choices: Sam is right: a bigger bottom number means more
Sam is wrong: the two fractions turn out equal
Sam is right: 3 pieces beats 2 pieces
quiz.explain: Both fractions refer to the same-sized whole. Over a common denominator of 40, 3/8 becomes 15/40 and 2/5 becomes 16/40, so 2/5 is larger. The denominator says how many equal parts make the whole; by itself it does not tell you which fraction is larger.

quiz.prompt: What is 3/4 of 20?
quiz.explain: One quarter of 20 is 5, so three quarters is 3 x 5 = 15.

quiz.prompt: Simplify 18/24 to its lowest terms. What is the denominator of the simplified fraction?
quiz.explain: Dividing top and bottom by 6 gives 3/4, so the denominator is 4.

quiz.prompt: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. You eat 3 slices and a friend eats 2. What fraction of the pizza is left?
quiz.explain: Five slices are gone, so 3 of the 8 slices remain: 3/8.

quiz.prompt: A recipe needs 1/2 a cup of sugar and you have 3/4 of a cup. How much is left once you measure out what the recipe needs?
quiz.answer: 1/4 cup
quiz.explain: 3/4 - 1/2 = 3/4 - 2/4 = 1/4 of a cup. Subtracting tops and bottoms separately would wrongly give 2/2.

quiz.prompt: What is 2/5 of 45?
quiz.explain: Divide 45 into 5 equal parts of 9, then take 2 of them: 2 x 9 = 18.

quiz.prompt: Simplify 30/45 to its lowest terms. What is the numerator of the simplified fraction?
quiz.explain: Both numbers divide by 15, giving 2/3, so the numerator is 2.

quiz.prompt: Ali multiplies 1/2 by 1/3 and writes 2/6, saying you add the tops and multiply the bottoms. What went wrong?
quiz.answer: He added the numerators instead of multiplying them
choices: He added the numerators instead of multiplying them
He needed a common denominator first
He should have turned the second fraction upside down
He forgot to simplify at the end
quiz.explain: To multiply fractions you multiply top by top and bottom by bottom: 1/2 x 1/3 = 1/6. Common denominators are needed when adding or subtracting fractions with unlike denominators, not when multiplying.

quiz.prompt: Which of these is a sound first step for adding 1/6 and 1/4?
quiz.answer: Rewrite both with twelfths
choices: Add the tops and add the bottoms
Rewrite both of them with tenths
Multiply the two bottoms and keep the tops as they are
quiz.explain: The smallest number both 6 and 4 divide into is 12, so 1/6 = 2/12 and 1/4 = 3/12, giving 5/12.

nodes.title: Decimals
nodes.goal: Compute confidently with decimal numbers.

quiz.prompt: Compute 0.75 + 1.6.
quiz.explain: Line up the decimal points: 0.75 + 1.60 = 2.35.

quiz.prompt: Compute 0.4 x 0.3.
quiz.explain: Multiply 4 x 3 = 12, then place two decimal digits (one from each factor): 0.12.

quiz.prompt: Jo says 0.089 is bigger than 0.7 because 89 is bigger than 7. Which reply is correct?
quiz.answer: Jo is wrong: 0.089 is less than a tenth
choices: Jo is wrong: 0.089 is less than a tenth
Jo is right: more digits means a bigger number
Jo is right: 89 hundredths beats 7 tenths
Jo is wrong: the shorter decimal is the bigger one
quiz.explain: 0.7 is seven tenths, while 0.089 is under one tenth, so Jo is wrong. But length settles nothing in either direction: 0.62 is the longer decimal and the larger number as well. Place value orders decimals; counting digits does not.

quiz.prompt: A pen costs $1.45. How much do 4 pens cost, in dollars?
quiz.explain: 4 x 1.45 = 5.80 dollars.

quiz.prompt: Compute 3 - 0.85.
quiz.explain: Write 3 as 3.00 and subtract: 3.00 - 0.85 = 2.15.

quiz.prompt: A ribbon 1.8 m long is cut into pieces each 0.6 m long. How many pieces do you get?
quiz.explain: Scale both numbers by 10 to get 18 divided by 6, which is 3. Dividing by a number below 1 gives an answer larger than you started with.

quiz.prompt: Compute 2.5 x 0.4.
quiz.explain: 25 x 4 = 100, and there are two decimal places between the two numbers, so the answer is 1.00, which is 1.

quiz.prompt: Round 3.478 to two decimal places.
quiz.explain: The third decimal digit is 8, which is 5 or more, so the hundredths digit rounds up from 7 to 8.

quiz.prompt: You buy items costing $3.40 and $2.75 and pay with a $10 note. How much change do you get, in dollars?
quiz.explain: The items total $6.15, and $10 - $6.15 = $3.85.

quiz.prompt: One scale shows a parcel as 1.2 kg and another shows it as 1.20 kg. Which statement is right?
quiz.answer: They show the same mass
choices: The second reading is ten times heavier
The second reading is a tenth heavier
The first reading is a tenth of the second
quiz.explain: A zero at the end of a decimal adds no value: 1.20 kg is 1 kg and 2 tenths, exactly the same as 1.2 kg.

lesson_media.alt: A place-value chart and number line show that 0.700 is greater than 0.089.
lesson_media.caption: Compare decimals from the highest place value; trailing zeros do not change the number.

nodes.title: Percentages
nodes.goal: Move between fractions, decimals and percents.

quiz.prompt: A jacket costs $80 and is marked 25% off. What is the sale price?
Write the fraction 3/5 as a percentage. Give just the number.
A test has 40 questions and you answer 30 correctly. What percentage did you score?
A $200 bike is reduced by 10%, and the new price is then reduced by a further 10%. What is the final price?
quiz.explain: The first cut gives $180, and 10% of $180 is $18, leaving $162. Two 10% cuts are not the same as one 20% cut.

quiz.prompt: Three shops advertise discounts on the same price: one takes off 0.35 of it, one takes off 3/8 of it, and one takes off 30%. Which discount saves the most?
quiz.answer: The 3/8 discount
quiz.explain: 3/8 = 0.375, which beats 0.35 and 0.30. Turning each one into a decimal makes the comparison easy.

quiz.prompt: A shirt's price rises from $40 to $50. By what percentage did it increase?
quiz.explain: The rise is $10 on an original $40, and 10/40 = 0.25, which is 25%.

quiz.prompt: What is 15% of 60?
quiz.explain: 10% of 60 is 6 and 5% is half of that, 3, so 15% is 6 + 3 = 9.

quiz.prompt: Write the decimal 0.07 as a percentage. Give just the number.
quiz.explain: Percent means hundredths, and 0.07 is 7 hundredths, so it is 7%.

quiz.prompt: A student works out 20% of 150 by dividing 150 by 20, getting 7.5. What should they have done instead?
quiz.answer: Divided by five
quiz.explain: 20% is one fifth, so you divide by 5: 150 / 5 = 30. Dividing by 20 gives 5%, not 20%.

quiz.prompt: A price goes up by 20%, and later the new price comes down by 20%. Predict how the final price compares with the original.
quiz.answer: A little below the original price
choices: A little below the original price
A little above the original price
quiz.explain: The rise is 20% of the small number and the fall is 20% of the bigger number, so $100 becomes $120 and then $96 - a 4% loss overall.

lesson_media.alt: Three-fifths, 0.60, and 60 percent are shown as equivalent parts of one whole.
lesson_media.caption: Percent means per hundred; the whole being measured still matters.

nodes.title: Negative Numbers
nodes.goal: Work below zero on the number line.

lesson_media.alt: A counter moves seven units left from negative two to negative nine on a number line.
lesson_media.caption: Numbers farther right are greater; adding and subtracting are directed moves.

lesson_media.title: Walk the integer number line
lesson_media.instructions: Choose a signed move, then apply it. Moving right increases the value; moving left decreases it. Use the arrow keys on the move control for one-unit steps.

quiz.prompt: Compute -7 + 12.
quiz.explain: Starting at -7 and moving 12 to the right on the number line lands on 5.

quiz.prompt: The temperature is -3 C and then drops another 8 degrees. What is the new temperature?
quiz.explain: Dropping means subtracting: -3 - 8 = -11 C.

quiz.prompt: Compute -6 - (-9).
quiz.explain: Subtracting a negative is the same as adding: -6 + 9 = 3.

quiz.prompt: On a number line, which single move takes you from -2 to -9?
quiz.answer: Subtract 7
quiz.explain: Going from -2 to -9 means moving 7 units to the left, which is subtracting 7.

quiz.prompt: Compute (-4) x (-5).
quiz.explain: A negative times a negative gives a positive, so the answer is 20.

quiz.prompt: A bank account is overdrawn at -$25. You pay in $40. What is the new balance?
quiz.explain: Adding 40 to -25 gives 15, so the account ends up $15 in credit.

quiz.prompt: Compute -15 + 8 + 4.
quiz.explain: Adding 8 to -15 gives -7, and adding 4 more gives -3: you are still below zero.

quiz.prompt: Compute (-24) / 6.
quiz.explain: A negative divided by a positive is negative, and 24 / 6 = 4, so the answer is -4.

quiz.prompt: A lift starts at level -2, rises 5 levels, then drops 1 level. Where does it stop?
quiz.answer: Two levels above the ground
quiz.explain: Start at -2, add 5 to reach 3, then subtract 1 to reach 2 - two levels above ground.

quiz.prompt: Which is the warmer temperature, -8 degrees or -3 degrees, and why?
quiz.answer: -3 degrees, because it is nearer to zero
choices: -3 degrees, because it is nearer to zero
-8 degrees, because eight is larger than three
-8 degrees, because it is further from zero
quiz.explain: On the number line, -3 sits to the right of -8, so it is the greater and warmer temperature. The minus sign matters: -8 has greater absolute value but is less than -3. The last option names the warmer temperature for the wrong reason, because -3 is greater, not smaller.

nodes.title: Order of Operations
nodes.goal: Evaluate expressions the way mathematicians agree to.

quiz.prompt: Evaluate 3 + 4 x 2.
quiz.explain: Multiplication comes before addition: 4 x 2 = 8, then 3 + 8 = 11.

quiz.prompt: Evaluate 2 x (5 + 3)^2 / 4.
quiz.explain: Parentheses first: 5 + 3 = 8; then 8^2 = 64; then 2 x 64 = 128; then 128 / 4 = 32.

quiz.prompt: Evaluate 20 - 3 x 4 + 2.
quiz.explain: Multiplication first: 3 x 4 = 12. Then work left to right: 20 - 12 + 2 = 10.

quiz.prompt: Two students evaluate 8 - 2 + 3. One gets 9 and the other gets 3. Who is right, and why?
quiz.answer: 9, because you work left to right
choices: 9, because you work left to right
3, because the plus sign binds more tightly
Both are right; the order is a matter of taste
quiz.explain: Addition and subtraction rank equally, so you go left to right: 8 - 2 = 6, then 6 + 3 = 9.

quiz.prompt: Evaluate 6 + 12 / 3 x 2.
quiz.explain: Division and multiplication rank equally, so work left to right: 12 / 3 = 4, then 4 x 2 = 8, then 6 + 8 = 14.

quiz.prompt: You want the expression 3 + 5 x 2 to come out as 16. What single change achieves that?
quiz.answer: Bracket the addition so it happens first
choices: Swap the plus and times signs
Bracket the addition so it happens first
quiz.explain: (3 + 5) x 2 = 8 x 2 = 16, whereas without brackets the multiplication goes first and the value is 13.

quiz.prompt: Evaluate 5 + 2 x (9 - 3).
quiz.explain: Brackets first: 9 - 3 = 6. Then multiply: 2 x 6 = 12. Then add: 5 + 12 = 17.

quiz.prompt: Evaluate (4 + 4)^2 / 8 - 3.
quiz.explain: Brackets give 8, squaring gives 64, dividing by 8 gives 8, and 8 - 3 = 5.

quiz.prompt: A calculator returns 14 for 2 + 3 x 4, but a student expected 20. Why do the two answers differ?
quiz.answer: The calculator multiplied before adding
choices: The calculator worked strictly left to right
The student squared the last number
The calculator inserted brackets of its own
quiz.explain: Multiplication is done before addition, so 3 x 4 = 12 and then 2 + 12 = 14. The student added first, which is what gives 20.

quiz.prompt: Where should a pair of brackets go in 12 - 6 / 3 so that the value comes out as two?
quiz.answer: Around the subtraction
quiz.explain: (12 - 6) / 3 = 6 / 3 = 2. Without brackets the division happens first and you get 10.

lesson_media.alt: An expression is evaluated with division and multiplication from left to right before addition.
lesson_media.caption: Equal-priority operations are handled left to right; brackets can change the order.

nodes.title: Primes and Factors
nodes.goal: Find factors, multiples and prime numbers.

quiz.prompt: Which of these numbers is prime?
quiz.explain: 53 has no divisors other than 1 and itself, while 51 = 3 x 17, 57 = 3 x 19, and 91 = 7 x 13.

quiz.prompt: How many positive factors does 12 have?
quiz.explain: The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 12, giving 6 in total.

quiz.prompt: What is the smallest prime number greater than 30?
quiz.explain: 31 has no divisors except 1 and itself, while 32, 33 and 34 all split into smaller factors.

quiz.prompt: Mathematicians agree that 1 is not a prime number. What is the reason?
quiz.answer: It has just one divisor, not two
choices: It has more than two divisors
It is neither odd nor even
It has just one divisor, not two
It is where the counting numbers start
quiz.explain: A prime has exactly two distinct divisors, 1 and itself. The number 1 has a single divisor, so it misses the definition.

quiz.prompt: Write 84 as a product of prime numbers. How many prime factors does it have in total, counting repeats?
quiz.explain: 84 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 7, which is four prime factors once the repeated 2 is counted twice.

quiz.prompt: Two buses leave a stop together. One returns every 6 minutes, the other every 8 minutes. After how many minutes do they next leave together?
quiz.explain: You need the least common multiple of 6 and 8, which is 24. Multiplying gives 48, a time they do share, but not the first one.

quiz.prompt: What is the highest common factor of 24 and 36?
quiz.explain: 24 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 and 36 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 3; they share 2 x 2 x 3 = 12.

quiz.prompt: A student tests whether 91 is prime by trying 2, 3 and 5, then stops and calls it prime. Which divisor did the student miss?
quiz.explain: 91 = 7 x 13, so it is not prime. You need to test primes up to the square root, which for 91 means going past 5 to 7.

quiz.prompt: What is the lowest common multiple of 4 and 10?
quiz.explain: Multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 and multiples of 10 are 10, 20; the first they share is 20.

quiz.prompt: A student claims that every odd number is prime. Which example settles the matter?
quiz.answer: Nine, which is odd but is three times three
choices: Nine, which is odd but is three times three
Seven, which is odd and has two divisors
Two, which is prime although even
Every prime above two, since those are all odd
quiz.explain: Nine is odd but splits as 3 x 3, so it has a divisor other than 1 and itself and is not prime. Seven and the other odd primes are instances of the claim rather than tests of it, and 2 speaks to a different claim entirely.

lesson_media.alt: Twelve forms several rectangular arrays, thirteen only one factor pair, and one has only one divisor.
lesson_media.caption: A prime has exactly two distinct positive divisors.

nodes.title: Ratio and Proportion
nodes.goal: Scale recipes, maps and mixtures.

quiz.prompt: A recipe uses 2 cups of flour to 3 cups of milk. If you use 6 cups of flour, how much milk do you need to keep the same ratio?
quiz.answer: 9 cups
quiz.explain: Flour tripled from 2 to 6, so milk must also triple: 3 x 3 = 9 cups.

quiz.prompt: On a map, 1 cm represents 5 km. Two towns are 8 cm apart on the map. How many kilometers apart are they in reality?
quiz.explain: Each cm is 5 km, so 8 x 5 = 40 km.

quiz.prompt: A recipe for 12 people needs 9 eggs. How many eggs are needed for 20 people?
quiz.explain: 9 eggs for 12 people is 3 eggs for every 4 people, and 20 people is five lots of 4, so 5 x 3 = 15 eggs.

quiz.prompt: A model car is built to a scale of 1:24. The real car is 4.8 m long. How long is the model?
quiz.answer: 20 cm
quiz.explain: 4.8 m is 480 cm, and 480 / 24 = 20 cm. Multiplying by 24 instead of dividing gives the much-too-big 11520 cm.

quiz.prompt: Paint is mixed 3 parts blue to 5 parts white. In 40 litres of the mixture, how much is blue?
quiz.answer: 15 litres
quiz.explain: The mixture has 8 parts in all, so one part is 5 litres and the blue is 3 x 5 = 15 litres.

quiz.prompt: Two numbers are in the ratio 7:3, and the larger one is 91. What is the smaller one?
quiz.explain: Each part is 91 / 7 = 13, so the smaller number is 3 x 13 = 39.

quiz.prompt: A drink is mixed 2 parts syrup to 7 parts water. How many millilitres of syrup are in 450 ml of the mixture?
quiz.explain: There are 9 parts in total, so one part is 450 / 9 = 50 ml, and the syrup is 2 parts: 100 ml.

quiz.prompt: Six identical books weigh 2.4 kg altogether. What do ten of the same books weigh, in kilograms?
quiz.explain: One book weighs 2.4 / 6 = 0.4 kg, so ten weigh 0.4 x 10 = 4 kg.

quiz.prompt: Two maps of the same park use different scales: one uses 1 cm to 200 m, the other 1 cm to 50 m. Which map draws the park larger?
quiz.answer: The 1 cm to 50 m map
choices: The 1 cm to 200 m map, because its number is bigger
The 1 cm to 200 m map, because it fits more detail in
Both draw the park at the same size
quiz.explain: Because each centimetre covers less ground. If one centimetre stands for only 50 m, you need four times as many centimetres to cover the same park, so the drawing is bigger.

quiz.prompt: In a class, the number of boys to girls is in the ratio 3:4. Which statement follows?
quiz.answer: Three sevenths of the class are boys
choices: Three sevenths of the class are boys
Three quarters of the class are boys
quiz.explain: The ratio splits the class into 3 + 4 = 7 parts, and boys take 3 of them, so boys are 3/7 of the class.

lesson_media.alt: A two-to-three mixture scales to six-to-nine by multiplying both parts by three.
lesson_media.caption: Equivalent ratios multiply or divide every part by the same factor.

nodes.title: Area, Perimeter and Volume
nodes.goal: Measure flat shapes and solids.

quiz.prompt: A rectangle measures 8 cm by 5 cm. What is its perimeter in centimeters?
quiz.explain: Perimeter = 2 x (8 + 5) = 2 x 13 = 26 cm.

quiz.prompt: A rectangular box measures 4 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm. What is its volume?
quiz.explain: Volume = length x width x height = 4 x 3 x 2 = 24 cm^3.

quiz.prompt: A triangle has a base of 10 cm and a height of 6 cm. What is its area in square centimetres?
quiz.explain: The area of a triangle is half the base times the height: (10 x 6) / 2 = 30.

quiz.prompt: Two rectangles each have a perimeter of 20 cm. One measures 8 cm by 2 cm, the other 5 cm by 5 cm. Which has the larger area?
quiz.answer: The 5 by 5 square
quiz.explain: The square covers 25 square cm and the long thin rectangle only 16, so equal perimeters do not mean equal areas.

quiz.prompt: A cube has a volume of 27 cubic centimetres. How long is one edge, in centimetres?
quiz.explain: The volume of a cube is edge x edge x edge, and 3 x 3 x 3 = 27, so the edge is 3 cm.

quiz.prompt: An L-shaped floor is made by cutting a 2 m by 3 m corner out of a 6 m by 5 m rectangle. What is the floor's area?
quiz.explain: The big rectangle is 30 square metres and the cut-out corner is 6, leaving 30 - 6 = 24 square metres.

quiz.prompt: A square has an area of 49 square centimetres. What is its perimeter in centimetres?
quiz.explain: The side is the number that squares to 49, which is 7, and the perimeter is 4 x 7 = 28 cm.

quiz.prompt: A cuboid measures 5 cm by 2 cm by 4 cm. What is its volume in cubic centimetres?
quiz.explain: Volume of a cuboid is length x width x height: 5 x 2 x 4 = 40 cubic centimetres.

quiz.prompt: A student doubles both sides of a 3 cm by 4 cm rectangle and expects the area to double. Predict what really happens to the area.
quiz.answer: It becomes four times as large
choices: It becomes four times as large
quiz.explain: The new rectangle is 6 cm by 8 cm, so the area goes from 12 to 48 square centimetres - both directions doubled, so the area grew by 2 x 2.

quiz.prompt: Which unit suits the amount of water a fish tank can hold?
quiz.answer: Litres
quiz.explain: Litres are a practical unit for a fish tank's liquid capacity. Cubic units also measure volume, while square units measure area and plain centimetres measure length.

lesson_media.alt: Two shapes share a perimeter but have different areas, beside a cuboid made from 24 unit cubes.
lesson_media.caption: Length uses units, area square units, and volume cubic units.

nodes.title: Powers
nodes.goal: Use exponents for repeated multiplication.

quiz.prompt: Compute 2^5.
Simplify 3^2 x 3^3.
quiz.explain: When multiplying powers with the same base, add exponents: 3^(2+3) = 3^5 = 243.

quiz.prompt: Compute 10^4.
quiz.explain: 10^4 = 10 x 10 x 10 x 10 = 10000, which is 1 followed by four zeros.

quiz.prompt: Compare 2^10 with 10^2. Which statement is true?
quiz.answer: The power of 2 wins, at 1024
choices: They tie, since both use 2 and 10
quiz.explain: 2^10 = 1024 while 10^2 = 100, so swapping the base and the exponent changes the value a great deal.

quiz.prompt: Simplify 5^7 / 5^5.
quiz.explain: Dividing powers with the same base subtracts the exponents: 5^(7-5) = 5^2 = 25.

quiz.prompt: What does 3^0 equal?
quiz.explain: Dividing 3 by 3 gives 3^0 on one side and 1 on the other, so any nonzero number raised to the power 0 is 1.

quiz.prompt: Compute 3^4.
quiz.explain: 3 x 3 = 9, 9 x 3 = 27, 27 x 3 = 81: four threes multiplied together.

quiz.prompt: Compute 2^3 x 2^4.
quiz.explain: You are multiplying three 2s by four 2s, which is seven 2s: 2^7 = 128.

quiz.prompt: A student reads 4^3 as four multiplied by three and writes twelve. Which check exposes the mistake?
quiz.answer: Counting fours: 4 x 4 x 4 is sixty-four
choices: Counting fours: 4 x 4 x 4 is sixty-four
Swapping the base and the small number
Adding three fours to reach twelve
Reversing it: twelve divided by four is three
quiz.explain: The small raised number tells you how many copies of the base to multiply, so 4^3 = 4 x 4 x 4 = 64. Dividing 12 by 4 only retraces the wrong step and confirms nothing.

quiz.prompt: Which is larger, 3^5 or 5^3, and by how much?
quiz.explain: 3^5 = 243 and 5^3 = 125, so the power of 3 is larger by 118. Swapping base and exponent changes the value.

lesson_media.alt: Four cubed is expanded as three factors of four, giving sixty-four.
lesson_media.caption: The exponent counts copies of the base in repeated multiplication.

nodes.title: The Coordinate Plane
nodes.goal: Plot and read points on a grid.

quiz.prompt: In which quadrant does the point (-3, 2) lie?
quiz.answer: Quadrant II
quiz.explain: A negative x with a positive y places the point in the upper-left region, Quadrant II.

quiz.prompt: Which of these points lies exactly on the x-axis?
quiz.explain: A point is on the x-axis when its y-coordinate is 0, as in (5, 0).

quiz.prompt: The points (2, 1), (6, 1) and (6, 4) are three corners of a rectangle whose sides run along the grid lines. What is the x-coordinate of the fourth corner?
quiz.explain: The fourth corner sits at (2, 4), directly above the corner at (2, 1), so its x-coordinate is 2.

quiz.prompt: A counter starts at (3, 5), moves 4 squares left and then 2 squares down. What is its new y-coordinate?
quiz.explain: Moving left changes x alone. Moving down 2 takes y from 5 to 3.

quiz.prompt: A rectangle has corners at (1, 1), (7, 1), (7, 5) and (1, 5). What is its area in square units?
quiz.answer: 24 square units
quiz.explain: The rectangle is 6 units wide and 4 units tall, so its area is 6 x 4 = 24. The 20 is its perimeter.

quiz.prompt: Point A sits at (-4, -1). Which move puts it into Quadrant I?
quiz.answer: Add 6 to x and 3 to y
choices: Add 6 to x and leave y
Add 3 to y and leave x
Add 6 to x and 3 to y
quiz.explain: Quadrant I needs both coordinates positive. Adding 6 and 3 gives (2, 2); changing one coordinate alone leaves the other negative.

quiz.prompt: A counter at (2, -3) moves 7 squares up. What is its new y-coordinate?
quiz.explain: Moving up adds to the y-coordinate: -3 + 7 = 4. The x-coordinate is unchanged.

quiz.prompt: How many units apart are the points (1, 4) and (7, 4) along the grid?
quiz.explain: The y-coordinates match, so the points lie on a horizontal line and the gap is 7 - 1 = 6 units.

quiz.prompt: A student plots the point (3, 5) by first going up 3 and then across 5. Which point did they actually mark?
quiz.explain: Coordinates are written across first, then up: (3, 5) means 3 right and 5 up. Reversing the order lands you on (5, 3).

quiz.prompt: A point has a negative x-coordinate and a negative y-coordinate. Where on the grid does it sit?
quiz.answer: Quadrant III
quiz.explain: Left of the y-axis and below the x-axis is the bottom-left region, Quadrant III; the quadrants are numbered anticlockwise from the top right.

lesson_media.alt: A path moves left three and up two to plot negative three, two in Quadrant Two.
lesson_media.caption: Read x first, then y; points on an axis are not inside a quadrant.

nodes.title: Data and Averages
nodes.goal: Read charts; compute mean and median.

quiz.prompt: Find the median of the data set: 3, 7, 8, 5, 10.
quiz.explain: Sorted, the values are 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, and the middle value is 7.

quiz.prompt: Find the mean of the data set: 4, 8, 6, 10, 2.
quiz.explain: The sum is 30 and there are 5 values, so the mean is 30 / 5 = 6.

quiz.prompt: Five quiz scores are recorded as 4, 5, 6, 7 and 68, where the 68 was a typing slip nobody caught. Which average best describes a typical score?
quiz.answer: The median, which is 6
choices: The mean, 18, which uses every score
The midpoint of the lowest and highest, 36
quiz.explain: One wild value drags the mean up to 18, above every real score, while the median stays at 6. The range measures spread rather than a typical value, and the midpoint of the lowest and highest score is worse still: it is built from the very outlier that caused the trouble, so it lands at 36.

quiz.prompt: Five students scored 12, 15, 15, 18 and 20. What is the mode?
quiz.explain: The mode is the value that appears most often, and 15 appears twice.

quiz.prompt: A bar chart's vertical axis starts at 90 rather than 0. What effect does that have on the picture?
quiz.answer: Small differences look dramatic
choices: The bars become easier to compare fairly
quiz.explain: Cutting off the bottom of the axis stretches small gaps into tall-looking differences, a common way charts mislead.

quiz.prompt: The mean of four numbers is 10. Three of them are 6, 9 and 12. What is the fourth?
quiz.explain: Four numbers with mean 10 total 40. The three given add to 27, so the missing one is 40 - 27 = 13.

quiz.prompt: Find the median of the data set: 2, 9, 4, 7, 6, 11.
quiz.explain: In order the values are 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, 11. With six values the median is the mean of the middle two: (6 + 7) / 2 = 6.5.

quiz.prompt: Six people have a mean age of 20. A seventh person aged 27 joins them. What is the new mean age?
quiz.explain: The six ages total 6 x 20 = 120; adding 27 gives 147, and 147 / 7 = 21.

quiz.prompt: A street of ordinary house prices gains one mansion costing ten times the rest. Predict the effect on the mean and the median.
quiz.answer: The mean rises far more than the median
choices: The mean rises far more than the median
The median rises far more than the mean
Both rise by the same amount
quiz.explain: The mean uses every value, so one huge price drags it up; the median only shifts along by one position in the ordered list.

quiz.prompt: On a pictogram one symbol stands for 10 cars, and a row shows two and a half symbols. How many cars does that row represent?
quiz.answer: Twenty-five cars
quiz.explain: Each whole symbol is 10 cars and the half symbol is 5, so the row shows 10 + 10 + 5 = 25 cars.

lesson_media.alt: Four scores cluster near six while an outlier at sixty-eight pulls the mean to eighteen; the median stays six.
lesson_media.caption: Outliers can move the mean much more than the median.

nodes.title: Letters for Numbers
nodes.goal: Use variables and evaluate simple expressions.

quiz.prompt: Evaluate the expression 3x + 5 when x = 4.
Evaluate 2(a + b) when a = 3 and b = 5.
quiz.explain: First a + b = 8, then 2 x 8 = 16.

quiz.prompt: If y = 5, what is the value of 2y^2?
quiz.explain: Square first: 5^2 = 25, then double it: 2 x 25 = 50.

quiz.prompt: Which expression means 'three less than a number n'?
quiz.explain: 'Three less than n' starts at n and takes 3 away, giving n - 3. Writing 3 - n reverses the order and gives a different value.

quiz.prompt: A rectangle is w cm wide and 3 cm longer than it is wide. Which expression gives its perimeter?
quiz.explain: The length is w + 3, so the perimeter is 2w + 2(w + 3) = 4w + 6. The expression w(w + 3) gives the area instead.

quiz.prompt: If 4n = 36, what is n?
quiz.explain: Dividing both sides by 4 gives n = 36 / 4 = 9.

quiz.prompt: Evaluate 5n - 7 when n = 6.
quiz.explain: Substitute first: 5 x 6 = 30, then subtract 7 to get 23.

quiz.prompt: If 3x + 4 = 25, what is x?
quiz.explain: Take 4 from both sides to get 3x = 21, then divide both sides by 3 to get x = 7.

quiz.prompt: A student writes 4 + n to mean 'four times a number'. Which expression do they actually need?
quiz.answer: 4n
quiz.explain: Writing a number straight against a letter means multiply, so four times a number n is 4n.

quiz.prompt: A taxi charges $3 as a fixed fee plus $2 for each kilometre. Which expression gives the cost of a ride of k kilometres?
quiz.explain: The per-kilometre charge is multiplied by the distance and the fixed fee is added once, giving 2k + 3.

lesson_media.alt: Three plain x cards become three plain four cards; four plus four plus four plus five is then combined as twelve plus five to make seventeen.
lesson_media.caption: Substitution replaces every occurrence of a variable with the same value before simplifying.

nodes.title: Linear Equations
nodes.goal: Solve and graph linear equations.

quiz.prompt: Solve for x: 3x - 7 = 11.
quiz.explain: Add 7 to both sides to get 3x = 18, then divide by 3 to get x = 6.

quiz.prompt: Solve for x: 2(x + 3) = x + 10.
quiz.explain: Expand to 2x + 6 = x + 10, subtract x and 6 to get x = 4.

quiz.prompt: A taxi charges a $3 flat fee plus $2 per mile. If a ride costs $17, how many miles was it?
quiz.explain: Solve 3 + 2m = 17, giving 2m = 14 and m = 7 miles.

quiz.prompt: Solve for x: x/3 + 4 = 10.
quiz.explain: Subtracting 4 gives x/3 = 6, and multiplying both sides by 3 gives x = 18.

quiz.prompt: A phone plan charges a fixed monthly fee plus $0.10 for each minute of calls. A month with 200 minutes costs $35. What is the fixed fee?
quiz.explain: The call charge is 200 x 0.10 = $20, so the fixed fee is 35 - 20 = $15.

quiz.prompt: Two people solve 5x + 2 = 3x + 14 and get different answers, x = 6 and x = 8. Which is right, and how can you tell without redoing the algebra?
quiz.answer: x = 6, because both sides then equal 32
choices: x = 6, because both sides then equal 32
x = 8, because both sides then equal 42
Both work, since the equation has two roots
Neither works; the equation has no solution
quiz.explain: Substituting x = 6 gives 32 on each side, so it satisfies the equation, and a linear equation like this has at most one solution. At x = 8 the left side does come to 42, but the right side is only 38 - checking a single side proves nothing, since the test is that the two agree.

quiz.prompt: Solve for x: 5(x - 2) = 3x + 6.
quiz.explain: Expanding gives 5x - 10 = 3x + 6, so 2x = 16 and x = 8. Distributing across the bracket before collecting terms keeps the two sides balanced.

quiz.prompt: You simplify an equation and reach the statement 4x + 9 = 4x + 2. What does that tell you?
quiz.answer: The equation has no solutions
choices: The equation has infinitely many solutions
quiz.explain: Subtracting 4x from both sides leaves 9 = 2, which is false for any x, so nothing satisfies the equation. A true statement like 0 = 0 would instead mean infinitely many solutions.

quiz.prompt: The formula C = 5(F - 32)/9 converts a Fahrenheit temperature to Celsius. Which rearrangement gives F in terms of C?
quiz.explain: Multiply both sides by 9, divide by 5, then add 32: F = 9C/5 + 32. Rearranging a formula uses the same inverse steps as solving a numerical equation.

quiz.prompt: A student solves 3x + 5 = 20 by dividing everything by 3 first and writes x = 25/3. Explain the mistake and give the correct value of x.
quiz.answer: Dividing by 3 must be applied to the whole of each side, and the student left the 5 untouched. Undo the addition first: 3x = 15, so x = 5.
quiz.explain: Inverse operations are undone in reverse order: strip away the added constant, then the multiplier. Checking 3(5) + 5 = 20 confirms the answer.

lesson_media.alt: A balanced equation is simplified by removing equal quantities from both sides until x equals four.
lesson_media.caption: Equivalent operations preserve the solution because both sides remain equal.

nodes.title: Slope and Lines
nodes.goal: Connect equations of lines to their graphs.

quiz.prompt: What is the slope of the line through the points (1, 2) and (4, 11)?
Consider the line y = -2x + 5. Which statement is true?
quiz.answer: It falls 2 units for every 1 unit moved right
quiz.explain: The slope -2 means the line goes down 2 for each step of 1 to the right; 5 is the y-intercept, not the slope.
choices: Its slope is 5, because 5 is the constant term
It rises 2 units for every 1 unit moved right
It falls 2 units for every 1 unit moved right
It passes through the origin, where x and y are 0

quiz.prompt: A line has slope 4 and passes through the point (2, 3). What is the y-value when x = 5?
A line passes through (2, 7) and (6, 7). What is its slope?
quiz.explain: The rise is 7 - 7 = 0 over a run of 4, so the slope is 0 and the line is horizontal.

quiz.prompt: Which line is perpendicular to y = 3x - 4?
quiz.explain: Perpendicular slopes multiply to -1, so a slope of 3 pairs with a slope of -1/3.

quiz.prompt: A line has equation 2x + 3y = 12. What is its slope?
quiz.explain: Rearranged, 3y = -2x + 12, so y = (-2/3)x + 4 and the slope is -2/3.

quiz.prompt: A line passes through (-2, 1) and (2, 9). What is its y-intercept?
quiz.explain: The slope is (9 - 1)/(2 - (-2)) = 2, so y = 2x + b; putting in (2, 9) gives b = 5. The y-intercept is the value of y when x is zero.

quiz.prompt: Which equation describes the line with slope 3 that crosses the vertical axis at (0, -4)?
quiz.explain: In slope-intercept form y = mx + b, m is the slope and b the y-intercept, giving y = 3x - 4. Swapping the roles of m and b is the usual slip.

quiz.prompt: Line A has equation y = 5x + 1. Which line is parallel to it?
quiz.explain: Parallel lines share a slope and differ in intercept, so y = 5x - 7 works. A negative reciprocal slope would give a perpendicular line instead.

quiz.prompt: A tank drains so that after t minutes it holds V = 200 - 8t litres. What does the coefficient of t tell you?
quiz.answer: The tank loses 8 litres each minute
choices: The tank loses 8 litres each minute
The tank gains 8 litres each minute
The tank holds 8 litres when full
The tank is empty after 8 minutes
quiz.explain: The slope is the rate of change: -8 litres per minute, so the volume drops by 8 each minute. The 200 is the starting amount, the intercept.

lesson_media.alt: A line falls four units over a run of two, giving slope negative two, and crosses the y-axis at five.
lesson_media.caption: Slope is vertical change divided by horizontal change; a vertical line has undefined slope.

nodes.title: Systems of Equations
nodes.goal: Solve two equations in two unknowns.

quiz.prompt: Solve the system: x + y = 10 and x - y = 4. What is (x, y)?
quiz.explain: Adding the equations gives 2x = 14, so x = 7 and then y = 3.

quiz.prompt: Solve the system 2x + y = 11 and x + y = 7. What is the value of x?
quiz.explain: Subtracting the second equation from the first gives x = 4.

quiz.prompt: Two lines have the same slope but different y-intercepts. How many solutions does this system have?
quiz.answer: No solution
quiz.explain: Parallel lines never intersect, so the system has no solution.

quiz.prompt: Solve the system 3x + 2y = 16 and x - y = 2. What is the value of y?
quiz.explain: From the second equation x = y + 2. Substituting gives 3y + 6 + 2y = 16, so 5y = 10 and y = 2.

quiz.prompt: Three adult tickets and two child tickets cost $37, while one adult and four child tickets cost $29. What does one adult ticket cost?
quiz.explain: Solving the pair gives a child ticket at $5 and an adult ticket at $9; checking, 27 + 10 = 37 and 9 + 20 = 29.

quiz.prompt: While eliminating variables from a system of two linear equations, you reach the statement 0 = 0. What does that tell you?
quiz.answer: The two equations describe the same line
choices: The two equations describe the same line
The system has exactly one solution
The lines are parallel and do not meet
quiz.explain: An identity like 0 = 0 means the second equation adds no new information, so every point of the line solves both: infinitely many solutions.

quiz.prompt: Solve the system 4x + 3y = 18 and 2x - y = 4. What is the value of x?
quiz.explain: The second equation gives y = 2x - 4; substituting yields 4x + 6x - 12 = 18, so 10x = 30 and x = 3. Then y = 2.

quiz.prompt: A farmer counts 20 heads and 56 legs among his chickens and cows. How many cows are there?
quiz.explain: With c cows and h chickens, c + h = 20 and 4c + 2h = 56. Doubling the first and subtracting gives 2c = 16, so there are 8 cows and 12 chickens.

quiz.prompt: A pair of linear equations in two unknowns has exactly one solution. What does the graph look like?
quiz.answer: The two lines cross at a single point
choices: The two lines cross at a single point
The two lines lie on top of each other
The two lines are parallel and distinct
The two lines share the same y-intercept
quiz.explain: A solution is a point on both lines, so a unique solution means one crossing point. Coincident lines give infinitely many solutions and distinct parallels give none.

quiz.prompt: You want to solve 3x + y = 12 together with 5x - 2y = 9 by substitution. Which opening step keeps the arithmetic simplest?
quiz.answer: Rewrite the first equation as y = 12 - 3x
choices: Rewrite the first equation as y = 12 - 3x
Rewrite the second equation as x = (9 + 2y)/5
Add the two equations to remove y
Multiply the first equation by 2 and subtract
quiz.explain: The y in the first equation has coefficient 1, so isolating it introduces no fractions. Substitution is easiest when some variable already stands alone.

lesson_media.alt: Three systems show one intersection, no intersection, and two coincident lines.
lesson_media.caption: A shared point solves both equations; systems may have one, no, or infinitely many solutions.

nodes.title: Quadratic Equations
nodes.goal: Factor, complete the square, use the formula.

quiz.prompt: Solve x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0.
quiz.answer: x = 2 or x = 3
quiz.explain: It factors as (x - 2)(x - 3) = 0, giving roots 2 and 3.

quiz.prompt: What is the sum of the two roots of x^2 - 7x + 10 = 0?
quiz.explain: The roots are 2 and 5, and for x^2 + bx + c the sum of roots is -b = 7.

quiz.prompt: How many real solutions does x^2 + 2x + 5 = 0 have?
quiz.answer: No real solutions
quiz.explain: The discriminant is 2^2 - 4(1)(5) = -16, which is negative, so there are no real roots.

quiz.prompt: The parabola y = x^2 - 6x + 5 has a lowest point. What is its x-coordinate?
quiz.explain: The vertex sits at x = -b/(2a) = 6/2 = 3, midway between the roots 1 and 5.

quiz.prompt: For which values of k does x^2 + kx + 9 = 0 have exactly one repeated root?
quiz.answer: k = 6 or k = -6
quiz.explain: A repeated root needs the discriminant k^2 - 36 to vanish, so k = 6 or k = -6, giving (x + 3)^2 or (x - 3)^2.

quiz.prompt: A ball thrown upward has height h(t) = -5t^2 + 30t metres after t seconds. When does it return to the ground?
quiz.answer: At t = 6 s
quiz.explain: Setting -5t(t - 6) = 0 gives t = 0 at launch and t = 6 on landing; t = 3 is when the ball is at its highest.

quiz.prompt: The parabola y = x^2 - 8x + 20 has a lowest point. What is its y-coordinate?
quiz.explain: The vertex sits at x = 8/2 = 4, and y = 16 - 32 + 20 = 4. Completing the square gives y = (x - 4)^2 + 4, showing the minimum directly.

quiz.prompt: Solve x^2 + 3x - 10 = 0.
quiz.answer: x = -5 or x = 2
quiz.explain: The factors of -10 that add to 3 are 5 and -2, so (x + 5)(x - 2) = 0. Watch the signs: a factor (x + 5) gives the root -5.

quiz.prompt: Rewrite x^2 + 6x + 1 in completed-square form.
quiz.explain: Half of 6 is 3, and (x + 3)^2 = x^2 + 6x + 9, which overshoots the constant by 8, so subtract 8. The half-the-coefficient rule is the heart of completing the square.

quiz.prompt: A rectangle is 3 metres longer than it is wide and has area 40 square metres. What is its width, in metres?
quiz.explain: With width w, w(w + 3) = 40, so w^2 + 3w - 40 = 0 and (w + 8)(w - 5) = 0. Only the positive root, 5, makes sense as a length.

lesson_media.alt: A parabola crosses the x-axis at two and three, matching its two linear factors.
lesson_media.caption: Factors, roots, intercepts, vertex, and discriminant describe the same quadratic.

nodes.title: Functions
nodes.goal: Treat rules as objects: evaluate, compose, graph.

lesson_media.alt: Two checkable function chains start at three: applying f of x equals two x before g of x equals x plus one gives seven, while reversing the order gives eight.
lesson_media.caption: Composition depends on order: g of f of three is seven, but f of g of three is eight, so composition is not usually commutative.

lesson_media.title: Compare composition order
lesson_media.instructions: Choose an input, then compare f followed by g with g followed by f. Follow each intermediate value to see why order can change the output.

quiz.prompt: If f(x) = x^2 - 3x, what is f(4)?
If f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = x^2, what is f(g(3))?
Which of these relations is NOT a function?
quiz.explain: The input 2 maps to both 5 and 7, so it violates the rule that each input has exactly one output.

quiz.prompt: If f(x) = 3x - 2, for what value of x does f(x) = 10?
quiz.explain: Solve 3x - 2 = 10, so 3x = 12 and x = 4.

quiz.prompt: The graph of y = f(x) is shifted 3 units to the right. What is the equation of the new graph?
quiz.explain: To reach the same height 3 units further right, the function must be fed an input 3 smaller, so x becomes x - 3.

quiz.prompt: The rule f(x) = x^2 sends both 3 and -3 to 9. Say why f is still a function, and why it has no inverse until its domain is cut down.
quiz.answer: A function may send different inputs to the same output; what it may not do is give one input two outputs. To obtain an inverse, restrict f to x ≥ 0, giving f⁻¹(x) = √x, or to x ≤ 0, giving f⁻¹(x) = −√x.
quiz.explain: Many-to-one is allowed for a function but fatal for an inverse. Restricting f(x) = x^2 to x ≥ 0 gives the inverse √x; restricting it to x ≤ 0 gives the inverse −√x.

quiz.prompt: If f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = x - 4, what is g(f(5))?
quiz.explain: Work from the inside out: f(5) = 11, then g(11) = 7. Composition applies the inner rule first.

quiz.prompt: The graph of y = f(x) is replaced by the graph of y = 2f(x). How does it change?
quiz.answer: Each point moves twice as far from the x-axis
choices: Each point moves twice as far from the x-axis
Each point moves twice as far from the y-axis
The graph shifts up by 2 units
The graph shifts right by 2 units
quiz.explain: Multiplying the output doubles every height, stretching the graph vertically away from the x-axis. Adding 2 outside the function would shift it instead.

quiz.prompt: If f(x) = 3x + 6, what is the inverse function?
quiz.explain: Swap roles and solve: y = 3x + 6 gives x = (y - 6)/3, so the inverse is (x - 6)/3. An inverse undoes the steps in reverse order; it is not a reciprocal.

quiz.prompt: Machine A doubles a number then subtracts 1. Machine B subtracts 1 then doubles. Use the input 5 to show the two machines differ, and say what this means about composing functions.
quiz.answer: Machine A gives 2(5) - 1 = 9 while machine B gives 2(5 - 1) = 8, so the outputs differ. Composition depends on the order of the functions: f(g(x)) and g(f(x)) are generally different functions.
quiz.explain: Composition is not commutative, so the order in which rules are applied is part of the definition of the combined function.

nodes.title: Polynomials
nodes.goal: Add, multiply, factor and graph polynomials.

quiz.prompt: Expand (x + 3)(x - 2).
quiz.explain: Using FOIL: x^2 - 2x + 3x - 6 = x^2 + x - 6.

quiz.prompt: What is the degree of the polynomial (x^3 + 1)(x^2 - x)?
quiz.explain: The highest-degree term comes from x^3 times x^2, giving degree 3 + 2 = 5.

quiz.prompt: Factor x^2 - 9 completely.
quiz.explain: This is a difference of squares: x^2 - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3).

quiz.prompt: What is the remainder when x^3 - 2x + 5 is divided by (x - 2)?
quiz.explain: The remainder theorem says dividing a polynomial p(x) by (x - a) always leaves a remainder equal to p(a) itself — no long division needed. Here a = 2, so the remainder is p(2) = 8 - 4 + 5 = 9.

quiz.prompt: A cubic polynomial with leading coefficient 1 has roots 1, 2 and 3. Which polynomial is it?
quiz.explain: Expanding (x - 1)(x - 2)(x - 3) gives x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6; the signs alternate because all three roots are positive.

quiz.prompt: A polynomial of degree 4 has a positive leading coefficient. What happens to its graph far to the left and far to the right?
quiz.answer: It rises in both directions
choices: It rises left and falls right
It falls left and rises right
quiz.explain: For an even degree the two ends go the same way, and a positive leading coefficient sends both upward.

quiz.prompt: In the expansion of (x + 4)(x^2 - 3x + 2), what is the coefficient of x^2?
quiz.explain: The x^2 terms come from x times -3x and from 4 times x^2: -3 + 4 = 1. Collecting like terms after multiplying every pair is the whole method.

quiz.prompt: Factor x^2 + 7x + 12.
quiz.explain: You need two numbers multiplying to 12 and adding to 7, which are 3 and 4. Pairs like 2 and 6 multiply to 12 but add to 8.

quiz.prompt: A polynomial has (x - 5) as a factor. What does that guarantee about its graph?
quiz.answer: It meets the x-axis at x = 5
choices: It meets the x-axis at x = 5
It meets the y-axis at y = 5
It has a vertical asymptote at x = 5
It has a hole in the curve at x = 5
quiz.explain: A factor (x - 5) makes the polynomial zero when x = 5, and a zero output is a point on the x-axis. Asymptotes and holes belong to rational functions, not polynomials.

quiz.prompt: A cubic polynomial has a negative leading coefficient. Describe the two ends of its graph.
quiz.answer: It rises on the left and falls on the right
choices: It rises on the left and falls on the right
It falls on the left and rises on the right
quiz.explain: The leading term dominates for large |x|; with odd degree the two ends go opposite ways, and a negative coefficient flips the usual pattern. Matching ends happen for even degrees.

lesson_media.alt: A factored cubic and its graph share zeros at one, two, and three.
lesson_media.caption: Factors locate zeros; degree, leading sign, and multiplicity control graph behavior.

nodes.title: Euclidean Geometry and Proof
nodes.goal: Prove things: congruence, similarity, circles, Pythagoras.

quiz.prompt: A right triangle has legs of length 6 and 8. What is the length of its hypotenuse?
quiz.explain: By the Pythagorean theorem, the hypotenuse is sqrt(6^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(100) = 10.

quiz.prompt: Two triangles are similar with corresponding side lengths in the ratio 1:3. What is the ratio of their areas?
quiz.explain: Areas scale with the square of the linear ratio, so 1^2 : 3^2 = 1:9.

quiz.prompt: Which of these is a valid justification in a rigorous geometric proof?
quiz.answer: Vertical angles are congruent
quiz.explain: A proof rests on established theorems, not on the appearance of a drawing, a measurement of one case, or a run of examples that happened to work.
choices: Measuring with a ruler shows they match
The angles look equal in the diagram
It holds in all the examples we tried

quiz.prompt: Two angles of a triangle measure 47 and 68 degrees. What is the third angle, in degrees?
quiz.explain: The angles of a triangle sum to 180, so the third is 180 - 47 - 68 = 65 degrees.

quiz.prompt: Two triangles have all three pairs of corresponding angles equal. What can you conclude?
quiz.answer: They are similar, though perhaps not congruent
choices: They are similar, though perhaps not congruent
quiz.explain: Equal angles fix the shape but not the size, so the triangles are similar; congruence would need a matching side as well.

quiz.prompt: AB is a diameter of a circle and C is another point on the circle. What is the size of angle ACB?
quiz.answer: A right angle, 90 degrees
choices: It depends on where C sits
quiz.explain: Thales' theorem: an angle inscribed in a semicircle is a right angle, wherever C lies on the arc.

quiz.prompt: A rectangle measures 9 cm by 12 cm. How long is its diagonal, in centimetres?
quiz.explain: The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 9 and 12, and 81 + 144 = 225, whose square root is 15. This is the 3-4-5 triangle scaled by 3.

quiz.prompt: In triangle ABC the sides AB and AC are equal, and angle A measures 40 degrees. How big is angle B?
quiz.answer: 70 degrees
quiz.explain: The base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal, and the three angles total 180, so each base angle is (180 - 40)/2 = 70 degrees.

quiz.prompt: Two triangles share two pairs of equal sides and one pair of equal angles that is not between those sides. Why does this fail to prove congruence?
quiz.answer: Two different triangles can fit the same data
choices: Two different triangles can fit the same data
Angles carry no information about congruence
Congruence requires the three angles to match
Side lengths must be measured before angles
quiz.explain: This is the ambiguous SSA case: the given angle can sit opposite either of two possible triangles. SAS works because the equal angle is trapped between the two known sides.

quiz.prompt: Explain why an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two interior angles that are not next to it.
quiz.answer: The exterior angle and its adjacent interior angle sit on a straight line, so together they make 180 degrees. The three interior angles also total 180 degrees, so the exterior angle equals 180 minus the adjacent angle, which is exactly the sum of the other two.
quiz.explain: Two facts each summing to 180 degrees are set equal to one another, and the shared adjacent angle cancels. This is a model of a short two-step proof.

lesson_media.alt: A triangle's exterior-angle theorem is justified by two angle sums of 180 degrees.
lesson_media.caption: A proof links givens to a conclusion through established definitions and theorems.

nodes.title: Trigonometry
nodes.goal: Sine, cosine, tangent — triangles and circles.

quiz.prompt: In a right triangle, the side opposite angle T is 3 and the hypotenuse is 5. What is sin(T)?
quiz.explain: sin equals opposite over hypotenuse: 3/5 = 0.6.

quiz.prompt: A ramp is 10 m long and rises at 30 degrees from the ground. How high is the top of the ramp, in meters?
quiz.explain: Height = 10 x sin(30 degrees) = 10 x 0.5 = 5 m.

quiz.prompt: What is the value of cos(60 degrees)?
quiz.explain: cos(60 degrees) = 1/2 = 0.5, a standard reference value.

quiz.prompt: In a right triangle, angle A has cos(A) = 0.8 and the hypotenuse is 10. How long is the side adjacent to A?
quiz.explain: Cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse, so the adjacent side is 0.8 x 10 = 8.

quiz.prompt: A 6 m ladder leans against a wall at 70 degrees to the ground. How far up the wall does it reach?
quiz.answer: About 5.6 m
quiz.explain: The height is 6 sin(70) = 5.6 m; using cosine instead gives the 2.1 m gap between the wall and the foot of the ladder.

quiz.prompt: A point on the unit circle sits at an angle of 150 degrees from the positive x-axis. What are its coordinates?
quiz.explain: The coordinates are (cos 150, sin 150) = (-0.87, 0.5): in the second quadrant x is negative and y positive.

quiz.prompt: In a right triangle the side opposite angle A is 7 and the side adjacent to A is 24. How long is the hypotenuse?
quiz.explain: 49 + 576 = 625, and the square root of 625 is 25. The 7-24-25 triangle is a Pythagorean triple worth recognising.

quiz.prompt: You know the length of the side opposite an angle and the length of the hypotenuse. Which calculation recovers the angle itself?
quiz.answer: arcsin(opposite / hypotenuse)
quiz.explain: Sine is opposite over hypotenuse, so the inverse sine of that ratio returns the angle. Cosine would need the adjacent side and tangent would need opposite over adjacent.

quiz.prompt: A surveyor stands 40 m from the foot of a tower and measures the angle up to its top as 35 degrees. Which calculation gives the tower's height?
quiz.answer: 40 x tan(35 degrees)
quiz.explain: The 40 m is adjacent to the angle and the height is opposite, and tangent is opposite over adjacent, so height = 40 tan(35 degrees). Sine would apply if the sloping line of sight were known instead.

quiz.prompt: A point on the unit circle lies at 210 degrees measured from the positive x-axis. What are the signs of its coordinates?
quiz.answer: Both are negative
choices: The x-coordinate is negative and the y-coordinate positive
The x-coordinate is positive and the y-coordinate negative
quiz.explain: 210 degrees lands in the third quadrant, where cosine and sine are both negative. Sketching the quadrant is faster than recalling a rule.

lesson_media.alt: A point at 150 degrees on the unit circle has negative cosine and positive sine.
lesson_media.caption: Cosine is the horizontal coordinate and sine the vertical coordinate on the unit circle.

nodes.title: Exponentials and Logarithms
nodes.goal: Model growth and decay; invert exponentials.

quiz.prompt: Evaluate log base 2 of 32.
quiz.explain: Since 2^5 = 32, log base 2 of 32 is 5.

quiz.prompt: A population doubles every 3 years. Starting at 500, what is the population after 9 years?
quiz.explain: 9 years is 3 doublings, so 500 x 2^3 = 500 x 8 = 4000.

quiz.prompt: A radioactive sample halves every 5 hours. What fraction of the original remains after 15 hours?
